appearance_facts.fact: The map displays the contiguous United States with state abbreviations. The color scale on the right indicates that dark red/maroon corresponds to 'Low' (0) and light yellow/cream corresponds to 'High' (100).
Missouri (MO) is colored light yellow/cream, which corresponds to the 'High' end of the legend (near 100).
Mississippi (MS) is colored dark red/maroon, which corresponds to the 'Low' end of the legend (near 0).
Delaware (DE) is colored light yellow/cream, similar to Missouri, indicating a high value on the scale.
Missouri (MO) is visually the lightest state on the map, appearing lighter than Delaware (DE) and significantly lighter than Mississippi (MS).

printed_facts.fact: Title reads 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
Legend shows a vertical gradient bar labeled 'High' at the top (100) and 'Low' at the bottom (0).
State abbreviations are printed in black text within their respective borders.

public_definitions: The routing criterion is the 'Highest incidence state in the dashboard'.
The goal is to open the record for the highest-incidence state.
uncertain: The exact numerical values for each state are not printed on the map, only the color gradient is provided.
